--- title: "金沢市 Revisited" author: "DK" date: "2026-01-29" draft: yes execute: echo: false warning: false messages: false categories: [ishikawa] --- Made a first visit to Japan when I was 38. It wasn't to a large, well known cities. It was a city in Ishikawa (石川県), a prefecture with population of 1.1 million, along the west coast of Japan. We were visiting a medical device manufacturing equipment vendor in outskirts of Kanazawa (金沢市)[^1]. [^1]: population 457,000 Mr Shimizu surprised us and met us at the Komatsu (小松市) airport[^2]. [^2]: population 105,000 I have never met him and knew him only because we work for the same global company. Whereas the BD-Korea belong to Asia Pacific Region. BD-Japan was an entity unto itself. He guided us to the town of business, Kanazawa. Took care of dining, a private chef that fed us continuous tempura, cooked to order. It was a magical beginning. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Made a pact with my children that we would visit the areas of their mission. First was a return trip to Japan, with my 3rd son, who served in the Fukuoka mission. As part of a return visit to Japan, we took Shinkansen (新幹線) from Tokyo to Kanazawa. The good feeling that I had as a first time visitor returned. On the shinkansen ride, shortly after Nagano, my son, began a conversation with a local person who used to be SCM executive. ![](images/20241005_133020.jpg) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Initial guide was a Japanese business colleague. 24 years later that guide was replaced by my own son. https://photos.app.goo.gl/vzNuWuHuSpLJHThx7 Had a chance to witness a performance at the train station. Performed underneath the modern interpretation of a torii (鳥居) gate. A rendition of local heroes and legends performed by the young and old. No tickets, no lines, just people choosing to stop and watch. We were invited to sip drinks and enjoy the show by the locals. Thereby supporting and continuing the tradition of the 加賀地方 (Kaga region) ![](images/20241005_162050.jpg) Thanks to people of Kaga region for you hospitality and sharing the community spirit.
